audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gave Aurora Level 1 while the content prose on the same page opens 'Riven owns the early game and you concede it'. Level 3 was given to Riven although the prose calls it 'a genuine skill check', and First item was given to Riven although whys[5] ends 'call it even'.
audit.why: Three rows contradicted their own explanation. The packet chart [Riven, Riven, Skill, Riven, Aurora, Skill, Riven] matches the prose row for row, and matches the 44.44% win rate over 81 games far better than a chart that hands Aurora the opener.
audit.corrected: Chart rebuilt to the packet chart across both layers, with ratings pulled in line (4/10 on her rows, 7/10 at level 6).

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes listed generic 'levels 2-3 (full pattern)' for Aurora and never mentioned Wind Slash.
audit.why: Blade of the Exile grants attack damage and range and a one-shot ranged Wind Slash. That is the spike that changes disengage maths for Aurora: The Weirding hops her backward, and Wind Slash still reaches her afterwards. Riven's other spikes are Ki Burst at 2 and her first bruiser item, which lets Valor tank a full Q rotation.
audit.corrected: Spike row rewritten to Ki Burst at 2, first bruiser item and Wind Slash at 6; spikes[1].text now warns that Wind Slash reaches you on the way out.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer never named a single Riven ability (flagged in the packet defects) — it said 'her Q dashes', 'her W stun', 'her E shield' throughout. Two strings also claimed Between Worlds makes Aurora 'untargetable to her from outside it' and lets her 'wall-walk her Q dashes'.
audit.why: Riot's text for Between Worlds describes damage, a slow, and an area Aurora can teleport across — no untargetability and no terrain traversal. The real, verifiable edge is asymmetric: the zone slows Riven while Aurora crosses it freely. Riven's abilities are Runic Blade, Broken Wings (13s, three casts, third knocks back), Ki Burst (11/10/9/8/7 stun), Valor (10/9/8/7/6 shield-dash) and Blade of the Exile (120/90/60).
audit.corrected: Real names and cooldowns written throughout both layers; the untargetability and wall-walk claims replaced with the slow-plus-free-crossing asymmetry.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns held placeholders — 'Your committal tool', 'Your ultimate' — and no numbers at all.
audit.why: The punishable window here is concrete: Ki Burst 11s at rank 1 against Across the Veil's 22s. Her stun comes back twice for every leap you have, which is why the leap is a reaction and never an engage.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with Ki Burst 11/10/9/8/7, Valor 10s and Between Worlds 140s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Broken Wings' third cast knocks back, and nothing in either layer mentions it.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'the third hit knocking back nearby enemies'. Displacement moves Aurora out of her own Between Worlds rift, which is the one place she wants the fight to happen. Standing on the rift edge during her third cast throws away the ultimate.
audit.corrected: Not written — I could not verify whether the knockback pushes a target out of the rift's area or whether the rift persists around her, so I left the text alone rather than assert it.

edits.before: Riven owns the early game and you concede it — at level 1 you're a single-spell mage with no movement ability while she dashes in with Q off your CS, and once she points W she adds a stun to lock you. Don't throw Q to poke when she's even slightly close: she'll Q-dash sideways to dodge the missile, then dash back in and trade before your passive spirits matter. Last-hit at max Q range, hold E (The Weirding) as your slow-and-disengage rather than burning it as poke, and treat levels 1-2 as survival, not trading.
edits.after: Riven owns the early game and you concede it — at level 1 you're a single-spell mage with no movement ability while she closes with Broken Wings off your CS, and at 2 Ki Burst adds an 11s stun to lock you. Don't throw Twofold Hex to poke when she's even slightly close: she'll dash sideways to dodge the missile, then come back in and trade before your passive spirits matter. Last-hit at max Q range, hold The Weirding as your slow-and-disengage rather than burning it as poke, and treat levels 1-2 as survival, not trading.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 still favor her shield-and-dash all-in, but level 6 is your one real window — Between Worlds makes you untargetable to her from outside the rift and lets you wall-walk her Q dashes, so drop it once she has already spent her three dashes and her E shield. Inside the rift the slow pins her in your Q-curse-and-recast burst, and a takedown resets Across the Veil. Outside that ult window, never sit in lane at half HP: the second your W leap is on cooldown she'll W-stun into Q3 and one-combo you, and your spirit sustain can't out-heal a full shielded burst.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 still favour her Valor-and-dash all-in, but level 6 is your one real window — Between Worlds slows her inside the rift while you cross it freely, so drop it once she has already spent her three Broken Wings dashes and Valor's 10s shield. The slow pins her in your Twofold Hex curse-and-recast burst, and a takedown resets Across the Veil. Outside that window never sit in lane at half HP: the second your leap is on cooldown she'll Ki Burst into a full rotation and one-combo you, and your spirit sustain can't out-heal a shielded burst.

notes: The packet levelChart matched Riven's prose row for row while the shipped chart contradicted it in three rows — good evidence the packet chart is the trustworthy one where the two disagree. Aurora's own full file spells her ultimate 'Between the Worlds' in phases[4].why and breakdown.late in every entry in my slice; worth one global pass. Riven is female and the boilerplate full layer calls her 'he'/'his' in tradeGood, breakdown.feeding, breakdown.late, report[3].t and report[12].t; I fixed breakdown.late only, since the same six boilerplate strings repeat across all 70 Aurora matchups and a scripted pass is the right fix. Same generator also writes 'a immobile drain bot' in tradeBad, dontsFull[2].d, breakdown.trading and report[3].t. NOT ASSERTED: whether Broken Wings' third-cast knockback can displace Aurora out of her own Between Worlds zone.
